title.narrative: Durable Solutions Through Community Resilience - IOM/FAO/UN Habitat
Hållbara Lösningar genom ökad resiliens hos lokalsamhällen - IOM/FAO/UN Habitat

description.narrative:
Programmet "Strengthening Resilience of Disaster Affected Communities through Durable Solutions in Oromia and Somali Regions of Ethiopia" ligger inom ramen för Durable Solutions Framework, och genomförs i samarbete mellan tre FN-organ: Förenta Nationernas (FN) Internationella Organisation för Migration (IOM), FNs Livsmedels- och jordbruksorganisation (FAO) samt FNs Program för Mänsklig Bosättning (UN Habitat).
Det övergripande målet är att bidra till hållbara lösningar genom förbättrade villkor för hållbar socioekonomisk återhämtning och fredlig samexistens mellan internflyktingar och värdsamhällen, med särskild uppmärksamhet på de mest utsatta, i kombination med stöd till lokala myndigheter för att stärka deras kapacitet att möta internflyktingars behov. Med vägledning av ett samhällscentrerat operativt ramverk syftar projektet till att uppnå föreslagna mål i enlighet med DSI-strategins nyckelområden, med insatser på operativ, planerings-, policy-, lagstiftnings- och institutionell nivå. Kopplingen mellan de tre specialiserade FN-organen kommer, genom samordnade integrerade tillvägagångssätt som syftar till att skapa rättsligt, materiellt och fysiskt skydd för fördrivna samhällen, skapa synergier mellan operativa aktiviteter för kopplingar mellan stad och landsbygd, fredlig samexistens, försörjning, tillgång till bostäder, mark , och egendom (HLP), och tillgång till grundläggande tjänster.

The programme "Strengthening Resilience of Disaster Affected Communities through Durable Solutions in Oromia and Somali Regions of Ethiopia" is under the Durable Solutions Framework, and will be implemented through the collaborative efforts of three UN agencies: International Organisation for Migration (IOM), United Nations Food and Agricultural Organisation (FAO), and the United Nations Human Settlement Program (UN Habitat). IOM will be the contracting partner, and the lead agency for the programme.
The overarching objective is to contribute to durable solutions through improved conditions for sustainable socio-economic recovery and peaceful co-existence of disaster-affected communities with particular attention to most vulnerable groups while strengthening local government capacity in responding to the needs of internal displacement. Guided by a community-centered operational framework, the project aims to achieve proposed objectives framed around the key pillars of the DSI strategy, with interventions at operational, planning, policy, legislative, and institutional levels. The linkage between the three specialised UN agencies will, through coordinated integrated approaches aimed at generating legal, material, and physically protection for displacement affected communities, create synergies between operational activities for urban-rural linkages, community cohesion, livelihood, access to housing, land, and property (HLP), and access to basic services.

The overarching objective is to "contribute to durable solutions through improved conditions for sustainable socio-economic recovery and peaceful co-existence of disaster-affected communities with particular attention to the most vulnerable groups while strengthening local government capacity in responding to the needs of internal displacement".
To promote the provision of sustainable support allowing for short to medium to long-term development, project operations are two-staged where activities take place both in locations of displacement identifying and supporting households with return, relocation, and (re)integration, while simultaneously intervening in hosting communities to support socio-economic (re)integration through a whole of society area-based interventions.
The programme has 4 specific outcomes, each UN partner responsible for one outcome each, with the fourth outcome being joint for ensuring complementarity, coordination, lessons learnt, etc.:
Outcome 1: Target communities are supported to relocate, return, and (re)integrate through the implementation of community-based planning and multi-sectoral recovery interventions aimed at building community cohesion and resilience (main responsible IOM)
Outcome 2: Enhanced economic status of the vulnerable members in the displacement-affected communities through facilitated opportunities for livelihood diversification options through on-farm and off-farm interventions and increased access to finance (main responsible FAO)
Outcome 3: Regional and woreda administrations can facilitate sustainable reintegration of IDPs through the woreda development (main responsible UN Habitat)
Outcome 4: The Governments capacity in mainstreaming durable solutions in its programmes is maintained and enhanced (All UN agencies)
The project targets 56,396 displacement-affected persons, including host-communities over 4 years and is implemented in the Somali and Oromia regional states of Ethiopia that experienced massive displacement in 2026 and 2017 along their respective borders due to inter-ethnic/-communal tensions and disputes, mainly related to land and water resources. The partners have included IDP camps, sites and settlements, as well locations where IDPs are relocated or returning to, altogether 8 sites:
Oromia regional state: Miesso woreda, Gende Buno; Babile woreda, Darer Arba, Qoloji; Chinakson woreda, Gella.
Somali regional state: Erer woreda, Magalo-ad; Awbare woreda, Awbare Relocation site; Kebribayah woreda, Dhurwale; Godey woreda, Bayahew.

sector.narrative: Facilitation of orderly, safe, regular and responsible migration and mobility

description.narrative:
This is a results reporting for mid-term review in 2025. A full results reporting for 2025 is due in spring 2026.
The project relocated IDP households, supported economic resilience, strengthened governance, and enhanced environmental protection in project sites for returns, relocations and local integration of displaced households and their host communities. Key initiatives included cash transfers, infrastructure development, peacebuilding, settlement planning, market access, and legal training, ensuring sustainable resettlement and improved livelihoods for displaced and host communities. Displacement solutions were advanced through rangeland restoration, livelihood diversification, and market access efforts. It provided wheat seeds, livestock distribution, and business training to thousands. Cash-for-work enhanced infrastructure, while peacebuilding networks fostered stability. Environmental initiatives included tree planting and waste management. Training programs strengthened governance, tenure security, and resilience-building, supporting sustainable integration and economic development across affected communities.
Key achievements in mid-2025
Outcome 1: Community Based Planning (CBP) and community action plans were effectively developed in both regions, facilitating a community-driven approach to identifying local needs. Community Management Committees (CMCs) were established, trained and engaged in community mobilization and monitoring. In Oromia women and vulnerable groups in CMC decision-making processes was observed. Both regions benefited from school rehabilitations and expansion efforts, with two projects projects implemented in each region (one in Somali and two in Oromia). Additionally, four water resource development and improvement projects utilizing solarization have been successfully completed and handed over to the respective woredas. Furthermore, sports-led peacebuilding initiatives have been facilitated to strengthen social cohesion between locally integrated internally displaced persons (IDPs) and host communities. The voluntary relocation of internally displaced persons (IDPs) from Qoloji IDPs Camp to Bayahow in Godey, Shabelle Zone was meticulously planned and effectively executed. It involved a series of prerequisite steps carried out before the actual relocation, including the voluntary registration of IDPs, site visits (go and see) to planned relocation areas, a reverification exercise for those who voluntarily chose to relocate, and the final relocation operations. This structured process ensured that IDPs moved under favorable conditions, with pre-arranged transportation, three daily meals, health assessments to confirm travel fitness, ambulance escorts, and a well-organized distribution of durable housing. To promote stability and harmony, peace committees were established and trained in both regions. Additionally, sports events were organized to strengthen social cohesion. Community-based inclusive peace committees played a vital role in conflict management and peacebuilding, facilitating community dialogues, peace conferences, and peaceful resolution efforts along the border areas of the two regions.
Outcome 2: On-farm livelihood interventions were successfully implemented in both regions, particularly focusing on small livestock such as goats and poultry. Many relocated households (HHs) who received cash transfers invested in asset accumulation, primarily livestock. Enhancing soil fertility and vegetation is expected to mitigate soil erosion, improve moisture retention, and boost agricultural productivity. A transparent process was followed in identifying grant recipients. In Oromia, cash-for-work activities saw strong community engagement, with significant participation from women and youth. Additionally, capacity-building initiatives, including dry land farming, were effectively carried out. Rangeland restoration efforts successfully covered 69% of the targeted land in the Oromia region. In the Somali region, some relocated HHs have proactively secured access to farmland and grazing areas from host communities (HCs), highlighting local acceptance and sustainable community integration. The rehabilitation of water points has improved access to safe and reliable water for livestock in the Somali region.
Outcome 3: Housing construction/upgrade for relocated HHs and returnees initiated in both regions. Capacity building training is provided in both regions. A plan is to install mud-block-making machines in Darera Arba (Babile) and Awbare town (Awbare) sites to support returnee and relocated communities. Waste collection materials provided to all project sites in both regions.
Outcome 4: In Somali region, a Durable Solutions Working Group (DSWG) forum was established at the regional level and helped coordination and advocacy. Two zonal DSWG are established. A Durable Solutions Strategy and a costed action plan also developed for resource mobilization.
